expr: (list (progn (set-match-data nil) (condition-case e (replace-match "x" t t "abc") (error (list (car e) (cdr e))))) (progn (string-match "\\(a\\)\\|\\(b\\)" "a") (condition-case e (replace-match "X" t t "a" 2) (error (list (car e) (cdr e))))) (progn (string-match "b+" "abbbc") (condition-case e (replace-match "X" t t "ab") (error (list (car e) (cdr e))))))
note: THE THREE WAYS IT IS AN ERROR, asked as values because the runner compares condition SYMBOLS and two of these three share one. Emacs answers ((error ("replace-match subexpression does not exist" nil)) (error ("replace-match subexpression does not exist" 2)) (args-out-of-range (1 4))). The FIRST is the surprise: with no prior match at all Emacs does not say `no match data', it says the SUBEXPRESSION does not exist -- group 0 is a subexpression like any other and an empty register has none -- so the no-match case and the absent-group case are THE SAME condition with THE SAME message, and the only thing that tells them apart is the SUBEXP argument echoed in the data (nil against 2). The third is a different condition entirely: match data that does not fit the STRING argument is `args-out-of-range' carrying the offending span. kg answered `void-function' three times before 26.2 and reproduces all three exactly now, the SUBEXP-as-written in the data included.
